In a long object literal, finding a property means reading the whole thing, and two branches that each add a property at the end conflict. This rule keeps the properties of object literals and destructuring patterns in alphabetical order, ignoring case, so that every property has one place to be.

- A spread, `...rest`, splits the object: the properties before and after it are sorted on their own, because moving a property across a spread changes what wins.
- In a destructuring pattern, a default value that uses another property keeps that property before it.
- `--fix` reorders the properties, and each one takes the comment above it along.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"perfectionist/sort-objects" = "error" # or "warn"
```

Every option, set to its default. The ones that are commented out are unset by default.

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"perfectionist/sort-objects" = ["error", {
  type = "alphabetical",
  order = "asc", # "asc" or "desc"
  ignoreCase = true,
  specialCharacters = "keep", # "remove", "trim" or "keep"
  alphabet = "", # string
  locales = "en-US",
  sortBy = "name", # "name" or "value"
  fallbackSort = {
    type = "unsorted",
    # order = <"asc" or "desc">,
    # sortBy = <"name" or "value">,
  },
  groups = [],
  customGroups = [], # list of objects
  newlinesBetween = "ignore", # "ignore" or number
  newlinesInside = "newlinesBetween", # "ignore", number or "newlinesBetween"
  partitionByNewLine = false,
  partitionByComment = false,
  partitionByComputedKey = false,
  styledComponents = true,
  useExperimentalDependencyDetection = true,
  # list of objects or strings, object or string
  ignoreCallbackDependenciesPatterns = [],
  useConfigurationIf = {
    # allNamesMatchPattern = <list of objects or strings, object or string>,
    # objectType = <"destructured" or "non-destructured">,
    # hasNumericKeysOnly = <true or false>,
    # declarationCommentMatchesPattern = <list, object or string>,
    # callingFunctionNamePattern = <list, object or string>,
    # matchesAstSelector = <string>,
    # declarationMatchesPattern = <list, object or string>,
  },
}]
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```js
const user = {
  name: "Ada",
  id: 1,
  email: "ada@example.com",
};
```

{/* bad */}
```js
const { name, id } = user;
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
const user = {
  email: "ada@example.com",
  id: 1,
  name: "Ada",
};

const { id, name } = user;
```

The spread keeps `theme` and `locale` apart, and `retries` uses `timeout`, so neither is reported:

{/* good */}
```js
const settings = { theme, ...defaults, locale };

function connect({ timeout = 1000, retries = timeout / 100 } = {}) {
  return { retries, timeout };
}
```

## Options

The rule takes one or more configuration objects. With more than one, the first whose `useConfigurationIf` matches the object applies to it.

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `"alphabetical"` | How to compare names. `"natural"` treats digits as numbers, so `item2` comes before `item10`. `"line-length"` sorts by the length of the property. `"custom"` sorts by `alphabet`. `"unsorted"` leaves the order alone and only applies `groups`. `"subgroup-order"` sorts by the position of the group inside a nested list in `groups`. |
| `order` | `"asc"` | `"desc"` reverses the order. |
| `ignoreCase` | `true` | Compare names in lower case. |
| `specialCharacters` | `"keep"` | `"trim"` ignores characters other than letters at the start of a name, `"remove"` ignores them everywhere. |
| `alphabet` | `""` | The characters in the order they sort in, for `type: "custom"`. |
| `locales` | `"en-US"` | The locale that `"alphabetical"` and `"natural"` compare names in. |
| `sortBy` | `"name"` | `"value"` compares the values instead of the keys. |
| `fallbackSort` | `{ type: "unsorted" }` | How to order two properties that the main comparison finds equal: `type`, and optionally `order` and `sortBy`. |
| `groups` | `[]` | The order of the groups. A nested list makes several groups count as one. Properties that match no group come last, or where `"unknown"` is. |
| `customGroups` | `[]` | Groups of your own: `{ groupName, elementNamePattern }`, `elementValuePattern`, `selector`, `modifiers`, or `anyOf` with a list of those. A custom group can also carry its own `type`, `order`, `fallbackSort` and `newlinesInside`. |
| `newlinesBetween` | `"ignore"` | The number of empty lines between groups, `0` for none. A `{ newlinesBetween }` entry in `groups` sets it between two groups. |
| `newlinesInside` | `"newlinesBetween"` | The number of empty lines between two properties of the same group, `"ignore"` to leave them alone. The default follows `newlinesBetween`. |
| `partitionByNewLine` | `false` | Sort each block of properties that is separated by an empty line on its own. |
| `partitionByComment` | `false` | `true`: a comment between two properties separates two blocks that are sorted on their own. A pattern or a list of patterns: only a comment that matches. `{ block, line }`: separately for `/* */` and `//` comments. |
| `partitionByComputedKey` | `false` | A computed key, `[key]: value`, separates two blocks that are sorted on their own. |
| `styledComponents` | `true` | `false` skips the object passed to `styled.div({..})`, `styled(Button)({..})` or `css({..})`, and a JSX `style={{..}}` attribute. |
| `useExperimentalDependencyDetection` | `true` | In a destructuring pattern, find the properties a default value refers to, except inside a function that runs later. `false` only finds them in the default value itself. |
| `ignoreCallbackDependenciesPatterns` | `[]` | Patterns of function names whose callback arguments don't count for dependency detection. |
| `useConfigurationIf` | `{}` | When this configuration applies: `allNamesMatchPattern`, `hasNumericKeysOnly`, `objectType` (`"destructured"` or `"non-destructured"`), `callingFunctionNamePattern` (the object is an argument of that function), `declarationMatchesPattern` (the name of the variable it is assigned to), `declarationCommentMatchesPattern` (the comment above that) or `matchesAstSelector` (an ESLint selector). |

The groups a property can fall in are `"property"`, `"method"` (for a function or arrow function value) and `"member"`, each optionally with `"multiline-"` in front: `"multiline-property"`.

### `type`

With `"natural"`, `"line-length"` or `"unsorted"`:

{/* bad {"options": [{"type": "natural"}]} */}
```js
const sizes = { item10: "10GB", item2: "2GB" };
```

{/* good {"options": [{"type": "natural"}]} */}
```js
const sizes = { item2: "2GB", item10: "10GB" };
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"type": "line-length"}]} */}
```js
const user = {
  email: "ada@example.com",
  id: 1,
};
```

{/* good {"options": [{"type": "line-length", "order": "desc"}]} */}
```js
const user = {
  email: "ada@example.com",
  id: 1,
};
```

### `groups` and `customGroups`

Put `id` first, then the rest:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"perfectionist/sort-objects" = ["error", {
  groups = ["id", "unknown", "method"],
  customGroups = [{ groupName = "id", elementNamePattern = "^id$" }],
}]
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"groups": ["id", "unknown", "method"], "customGroups": [{"groupName": "id", "elementNamePattern": "^id$"}]}]} */}
```js
const user = {
  email: "ada@example.com",
  id: 1,
  save() {},
};
```

{/* good {"options": [{"groups": ["id", "unknown", "method"], "customGroups": [{"groupName": "id", "elementNamePattern": "^id$"}]}]} */}
```js
const user = {
  id: 1,
  email: "ada@example.com",
  save() {},
};
```

### `newlinesBetween`

With `groups`, `newlinesBetween: 1` wants exactly one empty line between two groups and none inside one:

{/* bad {"options": [{"groups": ["property", "method"], "newlinesBetween": 1}]} */}
```js
const user = {
  id: 1,
  save() {},
};
```

{/* good {"options": [{"groups": ["property", "method"], "newlinesBetween": 1}]} */}
```js
const user = {
  id: 1,

  save() {},
};
```

### `partitionByNewLine` and `partitionByComment`

An empty line or a comment keeps what is above it apart from what is below:

{/* good {"options": [{"partitionByNewLine": true}]} */}
```js
const user = {
  id: 1,
  name: "Ada",

  createdAt: now,
};
```

{/* good {"options": [{"partitionByComment": true}]} */}
```js
const user = {
  id: 1,
  name: "Ada",
  // Timestamps
  createdAt: now,
};
```

### `useConfigurationIf`

Leave destructuring patterns alone and sort only object literals:

{/* good {"options": [{"type": "unsorted", "useConfigurationIf": {"objectType": "destructured"}}, {"type": "alphabetical"}]} */}
```js
const { name, id } = user;
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"type": "unsorted", "useConfigurationIf": {"objectType": "destructured"}}, {"type": "alphabetical"}]} */}
```js
const user = { name: "Ada", id: 1 };
```

### `styledComponents`

With `false`, the style objects of styled-components and Emotion are skipped:

{/* good {"options": [{"styledComponents": false}]} */}
```js
const Button = styled.button({
  padding: 4,
  color: "white",
});
```
